description: "Write a past-sandbox curriculum on Antistatic: a period of history replayed with a clock, with checkpoints, forecasting questions and the evidence revealed along the way."
---

Follow these instructions for: $ARGUMENTS

---

A curriculum is a release: checkpoints (historical dates learners move through in order), questions (each a market whose bars open at a checkpoint and close and resolve at later ones), and disclosures (evidence, results and explanations revealed at checkpoints). Learners see nothing before their clock reaches it.

The rules are [RULES.md](https://antistatic.exchange/sandbox/rules.md), referred to by ID (T for time and disclosure, Q for questions, S for sources, P for process); the format is the compact manifest, [manifest.md](https://antistatic.exchange/sandbox/manifest.md). Read both before writing. Don't restate the rules to the user; cite their IDs when one applies.

Building one:

1. `antistatic_create_curriculum_draft` with a slug, a version (`1.0` for a first release) and a title. New curricula are admin-only for now; for anyone else, say so and stop. It stays private to the user and the learners they add.
2. `antistatic_add_checkpoint` for each point in time: an opaque key (T6), a title and a date. Several checkpoints may share a date; they keep the order added.
3. `antistatic_add_question` for each question, in the compact format: a key, a title, `introduced_at`, a `market` (code, type, budget, resolution criteria, unit) and `curves` (bar keys, thresholds, opening probabilities `p0`, `closes_at`, `resolves_at`, outcomes). Word everything as of `introduced_at` (T4, T5, T7): what a well-informed person then would have asked, with criteria a named source settles (Q1) and opening probabilities from the evidence available then (Q4).
4. `antistatic_add_disclosure` for evidence and results, each at the checkpoint where it became public (T1, T2, T3).
5. `antistatic_validate_curriculum` imports the draft and returns errors (which block publishing) and lint warnings with rule IDs. Fix and add again: an entry with the same key replaces the earlier one.
6. `antistatic_publish_curriculum` once it is valid and the user agrees. A published release can't change; a later version replaces it.

The tools suit small curricula (up to 40 questions). Larger ones are pushed from files with the `antistatic sandbox push` command line, in the same format.

Outcomes stay with the author: don't reveal them to anyone playing the curriculum, and keep them out of titles, criteria, background and keys.
